classification.difficultyReason: The complement rule applies to three independent events. The student must convert 'fails' and 'works' wordings to a common form (A fails 0.1, B works 0.85, C fails 0.2), take B's complement, and multiply. This is one more event and one more conversion than the two-component defect question, but it needs no case splitting.

content.prompt:
A farm has three water pumps. On any day, pump A fails with probability $0.1$, pump B works with probability $0.85$ and pump C fails with probability $0.2$. Assume the pumps work independently of each other.
Find the probability that at least one pump works on a given day.

answer.worked:
The complementary event is that all three pumps fail.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{B fails})&=1-0.85=0.15\\P(\text{all fail})&=0.1\times0.15\times0.2\\P(\text{all fail})&=0.003\\P(\text{at least one works})&=1-P(\text{all fail})\\P(\text{at least one works})&=1-0.003\\P(\text{at least one works})&=0.997=99.7\%\end{align*}$$
